data-scan.name: Data scan
data-scan.navDesc: Two weeks, and you know where your data stands
data-scan.recognise: The data is there — in your systems, your exports, your spreadsheets — but the insights aren't. Every overview is pieced together by hand in Excel, the numbers depend on who made the file, and you know there's more in your data than you're getting out of it — just not where to start.
data-scan.promise: Within two weeks you know exactly what data you have and how reliable it is, have a target architecture with requirements and acceptance criteria you can build or tender from, and know what to tackle first.
deliverables: An inventory of every data source — and where the insights are made today, down to the Excel files
Quality findings per source: completeness, duplicates, and the fields that look reliable but aren't
A target architecture with requirements and acceptance criteria, and a roadmap with a build estimate per step
One definition per KPI, with an owner and the exact formula — verified against your sources
2–3 quick wins you can implement yourself

deliverableGroups.title: The map of your data landscape (as-is)
items: An inventory of every data source: system, owner, access, refresh cadence, volume
How data moves today: integrations, exports, retyping — and which steps are manual
Where the figures are made today: the Excel files, exports and hand-built overviews, and who maintains them

deliverableGroups.title: The quality of the data
items: Quality findings per source: completeness, duplicates, staleness
The fields that look reliable but aren't — verified inside the systems, not from what should be there
How the same customer, order or product lives in multiple systems — and which identifiers fail to link them

deliverableGroups.title: The target architecture, requirements and acceptance criteria (to-be)
items: A target architecture: one authoritative home per entity, one reporting layer instead of loose Excel files
A metrics-layer design: every figure computed once, in one place
Functional requirements and acceptance criteria, written so a builder can build from them — with an explicit out-of-scope list
A gap analysis and a twelve-month roadmap, with a build estimate per step — ready to tender

deliverableGroups.title: The KPI definitions
items: A decision inventory: which decisions the numbers must support, who makes them, and what goes wrong today
One definition per KPI, with an owner and the exact formula — and who decides when it's contested
Source mapping and a measurability check, verified inside the sources — a KPI nobody can populate isn't a KPI

deliverableGroups.title: Assessment and priorities
items: A maturity score you can re-score later to show progress
2–3 quick wins you can implement yourself this month

notIncluded: Building anything — pipelines, models and dashboards are phase 2
Process analysis: how work flows is the Process scan; this maps how data flows
data-scan.intro: The data scan is the fastest way to learn what to fix first — and the cheapest way to find out whether we're a fit. One to two weeks, a fixed price, and at the end a document you can act on with or without me.

steps.label: Week 1 — Conversations
steps.body: I talk to the people who put the figures together today and the people who steer on them. Which decisions the numbers must support, what can't be answered today, and where the definitions diverge.

steps.label: Week 1 — Into the systems
steps.body: I look inside your sources myself — and inside the Excel files where the reporting happens today: what's in there, how clean it is, how it fits together. No assumptions based on what should be there.

steps.label: Week 2 — Working it out
steps.body: The target architecture with requirements and acceptance criteria, one definition per KPI verified against the sources, the maturity score, and per roadmap step a build estimate of what it costs and what it returns.

steps.label: Week 2 — Delivery
steps.body: The full documentation handed over, the roadmap on the table, and the quick wins you can still implement yourself this month.

process-scan.promise: Within two weeks you know which processes are ready for automation or AI and which aren't yet — with requirements and a build estimate for the top candidates.
deliverables: A map of your key processes and where the manual work sits
Per process: automate with standard tooling, a genuine fit for AI, or better left to people
An honest AI-readiness check: what's possible now, and what has to be in place first
Requirements and a build estimate for the top candidates, plus a shortlist ranked by effort against hours saved
2–3 quick wins you can implement yourself

deliverableGroups.title: The process model of how work runs today (as-is)

deliverableGroups.title: The automation & AI opportunity map (to-be)

process-scan.intro: Everyone says you should be doing something with AI; the process scan tells you where that's actually true. One to two weeks, a fixed price, and at the end you know which processes are worth automating, where AI genuinely fits, and what's better left as it is.

problem.title: Where it actually breaks down
problem.card1Title: Every department has a different number
problem.card1Body: Revenue from the CRM doesn't match revenue from the books, and nobody knows which of the two you show the bank.
problem.card2Body: Two days of exporting, pasting and re-checking. Every month again — and one formula dragged one row too far goes unnoticed for months.
problem.card3Title: The AI plan is hanging in mid-air
problem.card3Body: There's an idea and there's budget, but nobody can say whether the data it needs is usable in the first place.
problem.closer: All three have the same cause: there's no foundation underneath. That's what I build.

services.title: The foundation first. Then the AI on top actually works.
services.subtitle: Most AI projects fail on the data, not the model. I build the layer underneath — and it's exactly the same layer your reporting runs on.
services.service1Body: From scattered spreadsheets to a reliable data foundation with dashboards that actually answer questions.
services.service2Body: Practical AI solutions: document processing, RAG systems, automations, and AI strategy that works.

process.step3Body: I build the solution: data pipelines, dashboards, AI tools, automations.

whyFreelance.title: Senior capability, no overhead
whyFreelance.subtitle: One person doing the work himself, with a background you don't buy off a staffing shelf.
whyFreelance.card1Body: You buy a result with an agreed scope and a fixed price. If it runs over, that's my risk — which is how an engagement should work.
whyFreelance.card2Body: At the police and in aerospace you work under hard privacy and information-security requirements. Privacy by design isn't an appendix to my proposal.
whyFreelance.card3Body: Since 2020 I've explained complex technology on Udemy to thousands of people without a technical background. I do the same at handover to your team.
whyFreelance.card4Title: I build myself out of the picture

open-data-warehouse.title: A star schema in the open, on data anyone can check
open-data-warehouse.sub: End-to-end ELT platform on Dutch open data: Python ingestion, dbt transformations and a documented Kimball star schema — with tests and CI on every pull request, built the way a platform team delivers it.
open-data-warehouse.f1Body: Two fact tables with different grains in one schema, each pinned down in a single sentence — because that's exactly where modelling goes wrong.
open-data-warehouse.f2Body: dbt tests and docs run on every pull request; a broken model never reaches main.
open-data-warehouse.f3Body: DuckDB in CI, Snowflake or Databricks with a profile switch — the modelling is the point, not the engine.

ov-streaming-pipeline.title: Real-time delays across Dutch public transport
ov-streaming-pipeline.sub: Streaming pipeline on the national OV feed: vehicle positions flow through Kafka, delay aggregates are computed in five-minute windows, and a live map shows where the network runs late — right now.
ov-streaming-pipeline.f1Body: GTFS-realtime vehicle positions consumed through Redpanda, with a dead-letter queue for events that don't parse.
ov-streaming-pipeline.f2Body: Delay per line and station in five-minute tumbling windows — correct under late and duplicate events.
ov-streaming-pipeline.f3Body: A Streamlit map of current delays, fed straight from the stream.

strafrecht-rag.title: Ask questions of Dutch case law — with sources
strafrecht-rag.sub: RAG system over court rulings: semantic search across judgments, answers formulated by an LLM, and every claim traced back to the ECLI it came from.
strafrecht-rag.f1Body: Every answer carries its ECLI references — from claim back to the underlying passage.
strafrecht-rag.f2Body: No relevant passage retrieved means no answer. The system doesn't improvise case law.
strafrecht-rag.f3Body: Retrieval quality is measured against a test set with LangFuse tracing — not a demo that went well once.

about.metaTitle: About me — data engineer at NLR and the Dutch police
about.metaDescription: Data and AI consultant with a background at NLR and the Dutch police, and thousands of students on Udemy. I build data foundations for reporting and AI.
about.name: Ruud Juffermans
about.intro1: At Politie Noord-Holland I applied data analysis, automation and AI within criminal law — an environment where a wrong figure has real consequences, and where privacy and information security are not an afterthought. Before that I built a wide range of data projects as a data engineer at the Netherlands Aerospace Centre (NLR).
about.intro2: Since 2020 I've published courses on Udemy, by now with thousands of students. Explaining complex technology to people without a technical background is the entire job there — and it's also most of what a client is actually buying from me. A dashboard nobody understands isn't a dashboard.
about.intro3: The same thing came back in both worlds: organisations sitting on valuable data without getting information out of it, making AI plans with no foundation underneath. I started this practice to close that gap — for companies that don't have a twenty-person data team.
about.pullQuote: I've seen what happens when data and AI work — and what happens when they don't.

privacy.metaDescription: Privacy statement of Ruud Juffermans — Data Analytics & AI Consultant.
privacy.title: Privacy statement

sections.title: 1. Who I am
sections.content: Ruud Juffermans, operating as Data Analytics & AI Consultant, based in Noord-Holland, Netherlands. Email: ruudjuffermans@pm.me.

sections.title: 2. What data I collect
sections.content: Via the contact form: name, email address, optional company name and your message. Via the newsletter: email address. I use privacy-friendly analytics (no cookies, no personal data).

sections.title: 3. Why I collect this data
sections.content: To answer your question and contact you. To send the newsletter you signed up for. To improve the website based on anonymized usage statistics.

sections.title: 4. How long I keep data
sections.content: Contact-form data is kept as long as needed to handle your request, up to a maximum of 12 months. Newsletter data is kept until you unsubscribe.

sections.title: 5. Sharing with third parties
sections.content: I don't share your data with third parties, except where needed for service delivery: Proton (email sending) and Buttondown (newsletter). These processors operate under data-processing agreements.

sections.title: 6. Your rights
sections.content: You have the right to access, correct, delete and transfer your data. You can also object to processing. Contact ruudjuffermans@pm.me for any of these. You can also file a complaint with the Dutch Data Protection Authority.

sections.title: 7. Cookies
sections.content: This website doesn't use tracking cookies. No cookie banner is needed.

sections.title: 8. Changes
sections.content: This privacy statement may be updated. The latest version is always available on this page.
